Meet the team

A presidential ticket focused on students.

Tunde Oye Modicious is the presidential candidate, with Bright Kwakye Amoasi as his running mate for SRC Vice President.

Bright is described in the supplied website draft as a KNUST student pursuing a Bachelor of Education in Junior High School Education, specialising in Mathematics and Information Technology. His experience in student representation has strengthened his interest in inclusive participation, clear communication and responsible leadership.

Before publishing: Add Tunde’s verified biography, and confirm all team details, roles and achievements before publication.
Our direction

A student voice that leads to meaningful action.

A clear vision for a student association that listens, communicates openly and works collaboratively.

“To promote a responsive, inclusive and accountable SRC that represents students fairly and works with the university community to improve the student experience.”
Key priorities

A manifesto centred on students.

These are proposed areas of focus. Specific commitments should be reviewed against SRC responsibilities, available resources and university policies before publication.

01

Academic Support

Promote stronger communication on academic concerns and advocate for practical support that helps students access learning resources.

02

Student Welfare

Listen to welfare concerns and work with the relevant university offices to improve how students receive guidance and support.

03

Campus Services

Encourage constructive feedback on campus services and follow up transparently on issues raised by students.

04

Inclusion & Representation

Make room for diverse student voices and strengthen opportunities for students to participate in SRC discussions.

05

Transparency

Support clear updates on SRC activities, decisions and progress so students can understand what is being done on their behalf.

06

Student Engagement

Build constructive channels for dialogue between students, student leaders and the wider university community.

From words to work

A practical approach to leadership.

Good representation requires listening, prioritising, communicating and following through.

✓
Listen and documentCreate accessible ways for students to raise concerns and share ideas.
✓

✓

✓
